definitions.explanation: A person who attended the same school. Often used as a modifier in compounds like {同窓会|どうそうかい} (alumni reunion).

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}とは{高校|こうこう}の{同窓|どうそう}だ。
examples.english: He and I are high school classmates.

examples.japanese: {同窓会|どうそうかい}に{出席|しゅっせき}した。
{同窓|どうそう}の{友人|ゆうじん}から{久|ひさ}しぶりに{連絡|れんらく}があり、{懐|なつ}かしい{話|はなし}で{盛|も}り{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: I heard from a school friend after a long time, and we had a great time reminiscing.

notes:
Literally "same window" ({同|どう} same + {窓|そう} window), referring to students who studied at the same place. Most commonly encountered in the compound {同窓会|どうそうかい} (alumni reunion, class reunion), which is an important social tradition in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同窓会|どうそうかい}: alumni reunion; class reunion
- {同窓生|どうそうせい}: fellow alumnus; classmate
- {同窓|どうそう}{名簿|めいぼ}: alumni directory

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {同級生|どうきゅうせい}: classmate — specifically someone in the same grade/year
- {同期|どうき}: colleague from the same entering class — common in companies and organizations
- {先輩|せんぱい}/{後輩|こうはい}: senior/junior — based on year, not just same school
